podcast.body: Released in 2002, the financial success of the "One by One" album enabled the Foo Fighters to invest a substantial $750,000 of their own money into establishing their own state-of-the-art recording facility, 606 Studios, in Northridge, California, around 2005. This studio became their central "all-purpose hub" for all band activities. "By the time the Fuzc got to the one by one album in 2005, they had enough money to invest in their own recording studio in Northridge, California."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 3

podcast.body: The release of this album was significantly delayed due to internal band struggles stemming from Taylor Hawkins's severe heroin problem and subsequent overdose in 2001. Dave Grohl temporarily stepped away from the band, and it was uncertain if the Foo Fighters would continue, but they eventually regrouped. "This is why the one by one album took so long to come out. Taylor needed to get his act together and Dave needed to step away from the band so he could sort his head out."
